feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant platform leadership experience. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited outcome-focused evidence beyond a few strong metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership brand: the headline and summary position you well for digital platform, communications systems, and governance roles.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions at NACo show trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good technical breadth with relevant tools/platforms; strongest impact comes where metrics are included (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles and projects: quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, search performance, email results, cost savings, or team impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use either “AI-enabled” or “AI enabled” consistently; standardize serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs lists without it); “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear public-sector relevance, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Use “website transformation” or “web platform modernization” for clearer, more current phrasing than “building the platforms.”
- If space allows, add a scale signal such as “10,000+ page sites” or “millions of annual page views” to strengthen specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Complex, mission-driven organizations” is effective but generic; avoid repeating similar broad descriptors elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper competency labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Clarify technical/strategic strengths without overlap: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: avoid mixing “systems,” “operations,” “infrastructure,” and “experiences” unless each signals a clearly different capability
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest value: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, communications, multimedia

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” closely duplicate the header and Topline Skills
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions and may be better emphasized elsewhere if space is tight
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner list format with parallel verbs and tighter phrasing; e.g., “Created AI-enabled legislative search combining hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Add 1 concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible for each project to increase credibility and specificity.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Consider shortening “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for ongoing campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search” overlaps with the current freelance role; keep this footer version shorter and more outcome-focused.
- “Advocacy Video Series” repeats video leadership already covered across multiple NACo roles unless you add a distinctive scope or result.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Modernized,” “Built,” “Led,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable context wherever possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative across legislative/member content, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve findability of complex policy resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consulting/embedded delivery and newer AI-search work.
- Drupal microsites and storytelling also overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer carry examples.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise ownership and clearer outcomes. Emphasize what changed under your leadership, not just what you oversaw.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed enterprise digital communications strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Rewrite bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email/social engagement, reporting speed, production cost savings from the studio, or efficiency gains from governance/publishing standards.
- Combine lower-value bullets for concision: merge analytics + governance into one operational-improvement bullet if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with older multimedia bullets; frame it here as capacity-building and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Sharpen it around scope, channel ownership, and outcomes that set up the promotion to Director.

Suggested edit:
- Open with progression + scope: “Promoted to lead NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletter ownership, launch/growth of weekly advocacy video, cross-functional editorial planning, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: subscriber counts, open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Use stronger verbs: “owned,” “launched/scaled,” “standardized,” “streamlined,” “coordinated.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the footer project; emphasize that here you scaled it into a recurring channel.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the Director role; frame this item as building the foundation rather than leading enterprise governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It would be stronger if tightened to distinctive leadership-level capabilities and framed with sharper, less generic wording.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with more specific, senior-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy and communications operations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content workflows
- Cross-channel campaign leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector and advocacy communications strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scannability and avoid repeating “leadership/strategy” language already used elsewhere.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas from 2022–present, especially governance, enterprise web improvement, and campaign platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats language already demonstrated in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-signal or older items from this topline section if not central to current targeting; keep SharePoint/Power Pages in “Technical + IT” instead.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “public-sector web platforms” to align with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal,” “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages” are already repeated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Studio operations

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”) and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, current capabilities rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery, not just tools: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows”

- If space allows, add scale/context instead of a generic tool item, e.g. “Studio buildout and live event production” given the NACo in-house studio achievement.

- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are partially redundant; combine them.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Use this space to sharpen relevance and signal depth in the platforms most tied to recent work, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency framing instead of a bare list, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcomes-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite and toolkit builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent use; it is less strategic than the other platforms and may dilute seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this section should add specificity, not restate categories.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier in parentheses or adjacent context elsewhere, e.g. **API integrations (analytics, CMS, search)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are the most distinctive items here—retain them if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show intent, not just tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Remove weaker/older tools unless they are current and used recently; prioritize Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “used to build cross-team workflows, approvals, and reporting processes.”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools and may add little value unless central to your systems work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add capability keywords instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey orchestration**
- Best combined version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • campaign automation • audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- If Dynamics 365/ Higher Logic were not used recently or materially, consider dropping the least relevant platform to keep this section aligned with your strongest recent experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills almost exactly. Use tighter phrasing and emphasize methods/capabilities that support the recent NACo and consulting work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Experimentation & Reporting**
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Swap vague **“Dashboarding”** for stronger, more specific terms like **“KPI reporting”**, **“performance analysis”**, or **“executive dashboards”**
- Order by strategic weight/recent relevance: analytics stack first, then optimization methods

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the topline version outcome-focused and this one strictly tool-based
- **SEO** and **A/B testing** are capabilities, not tools; if space is tight, move them to Core Competencies or keep only one skills section for methods vs. platforms

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-stage buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or frequency/volume of content.
- Tighten phrasing and emphasize hands-on delivery: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and coached a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- If metrics are unavailable, swap “high-impact” for specifics like “recurring,” “organization-wide,” or “member-facing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; position this item as launching or establishing the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital content and multimedia. Emphasize the distinct innovation/research scope and make the podcast launch the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the differentiator: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the digital piece: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and program work into member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast accomplishment sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid generic “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing; later roles already cover multimedia extensively.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital operations here, since stronger team/platform leadership appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. In Technical + IT, it should read more like specific tools/platform capabilities than broad function areas.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize software/tools: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast editing/production**
- Replace vague phrasing like **“Livestream studio workflows”** with a more technical label, e.g. **“Livestream production systems”** or **“Studio production workflows”**
- If accurate, add higher-signal tools used in recent roles (e.g. streaming/recording platforms, audio/video hardware ecosystems) rather than generic production terms
- Keep this item tool-focused; save outcomes and leadership impact for recent NACo/freelance experience bullets

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Podcast production** duplicates the older 2013–2015 role; keep only if podcasting remains a current capability
- Broad multimedia/livestream wording repeats other skills sections; this line should avoid restating category-level strengths
